analysis_refs.heading: Viewing the boards
analysis_refs.text:
**All records are samples.** Project Gutenberg IDs, titles and the Gutenberg
rights wording are real. Every paper, author, journal, DOI (the `10.5555` test
prefix), arXiv ID and children's story is invented. Never copy board records
into fixtures as if they were real catalog data.

analysis_refs.heading: 2. Scope
analysis_refs.text:
- Free to read: Project Gutenberg (local metadata import), Open Textbook
  Library and the bounded Book Dash catalog (owner-approved source expansion). Other free versions (LibriVox, Wikisource) appear only on detail
  pages as separate items, when a source links them.
- Papers: OpenAlex (when its key and budget are verified), Europe PMC, DOAJ,
  arXiv.
- Children's stories: the reviewed pilot set only, labelled as such.
- The library book page gains an "Also free to read" section.
- Desktop and mobile layouts, all three reading lights.

analysis_refs.heading: 3. Navigation and routes
analysis_refs.text: | Papers | Articles, preprints, chapters (`kinds` = article, preprint, chapter, thesis, report). Query field also accepts DOI and arXiv IDs. |

analysis_refs.heading: 4. Boards
analysis_refs.text: | `PaperResults` | Paper results with type pill, title, authors, container/year, and access line naming index and host. | Pill from `kind` (+ `version` for preprints: "Preprint · v3"). Source-supplied flags ("Correction listed", "Retracted") as a second pill in `--chk`/`--err`, worded as the source's claim. Access line: "Free · Found via [index], read at [host]" when they differ; "Free · HTML, PDF at arXiv" when the index is the host. Authors truncate to three plus "+ N". |

analysis_refs.heading: 3. Discovery engines to use before broad web searching
analysis_refs.text:
Also investigate DOAJ, CORE/OpenAIRE/BASE, national libraries, professional
associations and ministry directories as leads. Choose an aggregator only after
checking current external-use terms, quotas, origin attribution and completeness.
Existing direct arXiv/DOAJ deferral remains in force until its stated constraint
has a supported solution; this plan does not quietly re-enable those connectors.

analysis_refs.heading: Hosted release
analysis_refs.text:
No paid service/store was provisioned. Account resources, credentials, activation
and security settings are outside this change. Direct arXiv/DOAJ automation stays
deferred; the UI offers searches at their own websites.

analysis_refs.heading: Current free live profile — 2026-11-03
analysis_refs.text:
One source is queried at a time. Signed native cursors support Show more across
process restarts without server state. Replaying makes another live request;
live indexes can change. Source throttles/timeouts remain explicit. Direct
arXiv/DOAJ automation is deferred; use their source website search links.

analysis_refs.heading: Historical shared-store profile (superseded)
analysis_refs.text:
All controlled machines that dispatch arXiv requests, including previews and
production, must use the **same shared coordinator and namespace**. Separate
stores would defeat its aggregate pacing rule. Never use an in-memory store
for hosted live requests. Store failures disable live dispatch; local catalogs
remain independent. Provider 429 cooldowns are shared. Cached pages and records
can still be read while a new request would be queued/limited.

analysis_refs.heading: Historical shared-store profile (superseded)
analysis_refs.text:
The planner selects at most three live providers. Biomedical terms prefer
Europe PMC; general queries prefer the broad source and arXiv; DOAJ supplies
OA journal coverage. Recognized arXiv identifiers select arXiv. Sources not
chosen are explicit and can be searched independently from the source sheet.
DOIs select DOI-capable indexes; PMCIDs select Europe PMC using its PMCID field,
preserving the article's native MED identity. Bare versioned legacy arXiv IDs
also route directly to arXiv.
Language context is only supported by the broad adapter today; other paper
sources report unsupported rather than silently ignoring it.

analysis_refs.heading: Historical shared-store profile (superseded)
analysis_refs.text:
Search metadata is cached by exact source record as well as page. Opening an
arXiv result therefore uses the shared record cache instead of immediately making
another paced request. Licences remain attached to locations; a related journal
DOI is an access-unknown reference, never a substitute free copy.

analysis_refs.heading: Product requirements
analysis_refs.text:
- Search one selected paper source live. General searches use OpenAlex;
  biomedical searches and PMCIDs use Europe PMC. The Sources sheet switches
  sources. Explicit selection never silently searches a different source.
- Show more carries the provider's paging token in a signed browser token.
  Opening a result resolves its native record directly at that provider.
- No new database, Redis account, paid integration, shared cache or stored search
  session. Existing account features/resources are outside this change.
- Direct arXiv/DOAJ automation stays off because its aggregate pacing rules need
  coordination across deployments. Offer searches on their source websites;
  these connectors do not block other paper sources.
- Keep current source identities, verified free-reading rules, credits, versions,
  separate translations, source errors and browser shelf behavior.

analysis_refs.heading: Multi-source papers follow-up
analysis_refs.text:
DOAJ, arXiv and OpenAlex now have bounded adapters, source-native identities and
per-location access/licence handling. Fresh [policy observations](evidence/2026-11-01/source-policies.json)
verify DOAJ's 2 RPS and arXiv's 3-second/single-connection aggregate rules. The
configured OpenAlex key reported $1/day free allowance, $0.001 ordinary search
and zero prepaid funds; runtime rechecks those conditions before dispatch.
Operational limits and caveats are in [OPERATIONS.md](OPERATIONS.md).

analysis_refs.heading: Multi-source papers follow-up
analysis_refs.text:
The [actual paper flow](evidence/2026-11-01/papers-live-flow.json) exercised a
local API, actual Redis and official source metadata: 20 + 20 unique results,
source progress, reader → save → reload → reopen, and versioned legacy arXiv
lookup → reader. The latest first response took 2,468 ms across three sources;
the next buffered page took 198 ms. This does
not establish hosted performance or provider SLAs. No browser page errors
were recorded. The test facade initially hit an OS argument-size limit; using
stdin and adding the 180 KB check fixed the facade. The production REST protocol
does not pass cache values through a command-line argument.

analysis_refs.heading: Final source and refresh checks
analysis_refs.text:
All four paper adapters passed fresh [exact-record lookups](evidence/2026-11-01/exact-lookups.json)
without the record cache. Their observed times were 252–1,635 ms in this workspace;
these small samples are not SLAs. A fresh full paper flow also passed after final
changes: source progress, 20 + 20 unique records, save/reload/reopen and legacy
arXiv version lookup. The [flow report](evidence/2026-11-01/papers-live-flow.json)
records actual statuses and timing.

analysis_refs.heading: Final source and refresh checks
analysis_refs.text:
[HEAD/header-only sampling](evidence/2026-11-01/host-head-checks.json) returned
200 from the textbook, DOAJ publisher, arXiv and Europe PMC hosts. It found a
Gutenberg legacy HTML 404; GET response headers confirmed it. The supplied direct
HTML and EPUB routes returned 200. Importer v2 removes virtual HTML links and
uses supplied direct HTML/landing URLs; a fresh 1,000-record import and runtime
audit passed. The primary location's licence and downloads now stay together;
other hosts/versions retain their own licence, and retraction flags appear on
direct detail visits. No full-text content was stored.

analysis_refs.heading: 3. Canonical model
analysis_refs.text:
1. Normalize exact DOI, ISBN-10/13 equivalence, PMID/PMCID and provider IDs. Valid DOI syntax does not establish existence.
2. Reconcile descriptions of the same identified version, retaining all locations and provenance. Conflicting authoritative metadata goes to review.
3. Keep translations, editions, chapters, abridgements and recordings separate. ISBN is edition-level; ISSN container-level. Missing ISBN is valid.
4. Preserve arXiv versions and Zenodo version DOI separately from concept/unversioned identifiers. Preprint and journal article can be related without being identical. Relations require source evidence.
5. Use title/author similarity only for candidate review or visual grouping, never authoritative merging.
6. Assign durable app IDs to persisted records; alias older source-native keys rather than breaking links after reconciliation.

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Search and item resolution
analysis_refs.text:
1. Validate query length, filters, page size (initial max 40), country and cursor binding. Detect ISBN/DOI/arXiv/PMCID before broad search. Country is access context, not legal assurance.
2. Choose providers by user scope/capabilities. Books start from local catalogs; papers use OpenAlex when configured plus at most two relevant specialists. Without the broad index, disclose narrower DOAJ/Europe PMC/arXiv coverage.
3. Use shared cached results. Acquire global quota tokens for uncached requests; arXiv pacing includes all replicas/jobs. Skip with explicit status if the queue cannot run before the deadline.
4. Bound fan-out: proposed 5-second total search deadline, shorter per-provider limits where feasible, at most 3 live providers and one source page each. These are design targets, not measured guarantees. Busy arXiv queues cannot delay every result indefinitely.
5. Map, filter, reconcile and rank. Avoid detail requests for every hit; resolve uncertain access for bounded visible candidates or on item open. Unknown candidates cannot be advertised as free.
6. Return items, source statuses and freshness. Empty, timeout, throttled, quota-exhausted, unsupported and disabled differ. If all sources fail with no local/cached result, return retriable unavailable, not zero matches.
7. On item open, enrich locations as needed; surface editions/versions and host actions. Cache bibliography separately from access observations.

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Search and item resolution
Phase B — initial coverage
analysis_refs.text: Add Open Textbook Library, DOAJ and arXiv; OpenAlex after key/budget verification. Then DOAB/OAPEN imports and optional Unpaywall resolver with real contact email. Keep Google/Open Library enrichment bounded.

analysis_refs.heading: Phase C — children, regional and specialist coverage
analysis_refs.text:
- Provider contracts: valid/empty/malformed response, missing fields, absent license, preview/borrow/embargo, stale links, 429/503 and schema drift.
- Identity: same DOI across indexes, preprint vs publication, arXiv versions, translations, chapter vs book, missing ISBN, unrelated same title, Zenodo concept vs version DOI.
- Search: partial/all-source failure, exhausted budget, unsupported filters, cancellation, no skipped/duplicate pages, expired cursor, honest totals.
- Imports: interrupted/repeated OAI page, tombstone, expired token, corrupt/empty bulk file and rollback.
- End-to-end: title/author/DOI, free filters, details, external HTML/reader/PDF/EPUB where offered, browser back, unchanged ISBN/library/shelf flows; launch-country checks beyond server-region behavior.
- Capacity: uncached searches/day and peak concurrency. At the observed OpenAlex price, ordinary search cost is uncached calls × $0.001; paging/enrichment add requests. arXiv 1/3 sec is at most 20/min before contention. Configure degradation before enabling traffic.

analysis_refs.heading: C07 — Preprints and working papers
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval strategy.** Prefer existing attributed aggregator search where its
coverage passes. The [bioRxiv/medRxiv API documentation](https://api.biorxiv.org/)
supports date-window/DOI metadata retrieval and version information; it is not a
generic keyword search interface. A permitted bounded metadata import can make
that feed searchable locally. [RePEc's metadata policy](https://ideas.repec.org/getdata.html)
prefers publisher archives/ReDIF over website scraping and requires prior contact
for commercial use. Review applicability before use; no outreach is sent as part
of this plan. Direct arXiv automation remains deferred under the current plan.

analysis_refs.heading: C15 — Historical documents, manuscripts and archives
analysis_refs.text:
**Where to start.** Use [Archives Portal Europe's institution directory](https://www.archivesportaleurope.net/find-an-institution/)
to branch by country and holding institution. Its current page directs researchers
to institution search while directory work continues. In the US,
[NARA's Catalog API documentation](https://www.archives.gov/research/catalog/help/api)
describes keyword/search-result and individual-record JSON retrieval. Extend
discovery through state archives, university special collections and municipal
archive directories. In India, the National Archives'
[Abhilekh Patal description](https://nationalarchives.nic.in/en/online-portal-abhilekh-patal)
is the national starting point; follow state archives, regional record centers
and university manuscript collections separately.

analysis_refs.heading: C15 — Historical documents, manuscripts and archives
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval and tests.** Prefer supported archival search or licensed EAD/OAI
exports with origin attribution. NARA documents a machine route; current key,
terms and limits still require review. Abhilekh Patal's external integration route
is unverified here. A finding aid may describe an undigitized box: require an
actual digitized object for usable online access. Test collection → series → item
hierarchy, reference code, date range, historical place aliases and a multipage
object. A IIIF manifest can describe/display a known object; separately prove
catalog discovery. Flag missing OCR rather than promising handwritten full-text
search. Deep-review one supported catalog and one Indian-origin candidate first.

analysis_refs.heading: 2. Scope
analysis_refs.text:
- Free to read: Project Gutenberg (local metadata import), Open Textbook
  Library and the bounded Book Dash catalog (owner-approved source expansion). Other free versions (LibriVox, Wikisource) appear only on detail
  pages as separate items, when a source links them.
- Papers: OpenAlex (when its key and budget are verified), Europe PMC, DOAJ,
  arXiv.
- Children's stories: the reviewed pilot set only, labelled as such.
- The library book page gains an "Also free to read" section.
- Desktop and mobile layouts, all three reading lights.

analysis_refs.heading: FCD01: contract decisions
analysis_refs.text:
- Content keys use `fcd:v1:<source>:<record>`; Gutenberg records are positive
  integer IDs; Europe PMC records include their source (`MED`, `PMC`, `PPR`).
  A DOI is an identifier, never an app key. Versions, translations, chapters and
  recordings retain distinct source-native keys. No fuzzy-title merge.
- Reviewed StoryWeaver translations use distinct native story IDs. The pilot
  requires English/Hindi/Tamil records with original credits, publisher levels
  and per-record review evidence before enablement.
- An omitted `kinds` searches books/learning resources. Paper searches supply
  paper kinds explicitly. Mixed book/paper requests are reported unsupported;
  the API never silently omits one requested scope.
- Search and resolve both accept `country` (ISO alpha-2 or absent/unknown) and
  language context. An observation for one explicit country does not establish
  availability in another. Gutenberg's US rights statement is retained with a
  generic country-rules prompt, not turned into a global legal claim.
- A reading action requires an explicit per-location `free_full_text` claim,
  positive evidence field/source/time, a safe supplied HTTP(S) URL, and an
  observation no older than 24 hours. Stale, missing, contradictory or
  country-mismatched observations become unknown; fetch failure is not absence.
  Reuse licence and free reading remain distinct. Missing licence never becomes
  an invented Creative Commons licence.
- `not_selected` means the planner did not query this source; `disabled` means
  it is not connected. `ok` with zero results is distinct from timeout,
  unavailable, throttled and quota-exhausted. Counts describe loaded items,
  never a federated global total.
- Default results contain anonymous free full text and a separately labelled verified free-account group (owner clarification 2026-11-01). An explicit unclear group may
  contain unknown/metadata-only items with labelled source links; previews,
  borrowing, unknown-price registration and restricted access stay excluded in v1.
- Source cursors remain server-owned. Browser tokens bind query, context,
  policy/index revisions and expiry. Shared live quota reservation and page
  advancement must pass a two-instance test before a live source is enabled.
  A memory implementation is a development/test adapter only; store failure
  disables uncapped live dispatch while keeping local metadata searchable.

analysis_refs.text:
The planner selects at most three live providers. Biomedical terms prefer
Europe PMC; general queries prefer the broad source and arXiv; DOAJ supplies
OA journal coverage. Recognized arXiv identifiers select arXiv. Sources not

analysis_refs.heading: Free-content production release
analysis_refs.text:
**Current revision (2026-11-03):** the owner authorized the
[simple free live plan](SIMPLE_LIVE_PLAN.md), #156. Release/hosted verification is
tracked in #159. Europe PMC/OpenAlex can run directly with no data store; the
blanket Redis gate is superseded. This release must retain verified free-budget
guards and existing account settings. The November 1 evidence below records the
initial book release, rather than the current paper prerequisites.

analysis_refs.heading: Product requirements
analysis_refs.text:
- Search one selected paper source live. General searches use OpenAlex;
  biomedical searches and PMCIDs use Europe PMC. The Sources sheet switches
  sources. Explicit selection never silently searches a different source.
- Show more carries the provider's paging token in a signed browser token.
  Opening a result resolves its native record directly at that provider.
- No new database, Redis account, paid integration, shared cache or stored search
  session. Existing account features/resources are outside this change.
- Direct arXiv/DOAJ automation stays off because its aggregate pacing rules need
  coordination across deployments. Offer searches on their source websites;
  these connectors do not block other paper sources.
- Keep current source identities, verified free-reading rules, credits, versions,
  separate translations, source errors and browser shelf behavior.

analysis_refs.heading: Cost and limits
analysis_refs.text:
Europe PMC uses its public API. OpenAlex uses the existing server-only key;
verify its free allowance, accepted endpoint pricing and zero prepaid balance
before dispatch. Exhaustion, paid balances or unknown policy stop the request.
No paid fallback or paid infrastructure is introduced. Normal hosting usage
continues under the existing Vercel plan; future hosting costs are not guaranteed
to be zero.

analysis_refs.heading: Configuration and delivery
analysis_refs.text:
Keep the existing discovery flag and strong cursor signer. Enable Europe PMC
and optionally OpenAlex with its key. Remove Redis and per-source application
daily/minute budget variables from active setup. No client-exposed credentials
or database migration.

analysis_refs.heading: Evidence and limits
analysis_refs.text:
- The comparison fixtures are explicitly synthetic for papers/stories; they do
  not establish source access or represent the actual reviewed children's set.
  Their metadata is isolated in `client/e2e/free-content-ui-fixture.js`.
- The [actual-source app flows](evidence/2026-11-01/ui-review/actual-source-flow/expanded-sources-app-flow.json)
  separately exercise the real Tamil StoryWeaver record and Book Dash edition:
  search → detail → supplied source URL → save → reload → reopen, on desktop and
  phone, including 320px/200% text. Their credits and free-account condition are
  preserved. No source account was created and post-login reading is untested.
- Sources, counts, levels and available relations differ from the board samples.
  Only source-supplied versions/downloads/relations render; no v1/v2 list, recording,
  translation, cover art or licence is inferred to imitate sample data.
- The shared four-tab shell, desktop navigation rail and browser safe-area
  handling remain the existing app. The source sheet keeps its shared Close
  control. Catalog-subset disclosure and the owner-approved free-account group
  add necessary content beyond the original sample boards.
- Recent query history is bounded and lost on reload. It is not written to
  local storage, an account, analytics or a server history store.
- A fresh Europe PMC request on the current local API exceeded the five-second
  source deadline. The actual UI rendered an unavailable alert and no empty-copy
  claim. Earlier successful live-paper flows remain dated evidence, not a claim
  that the external service answered this later probe.
- The streamed-loading fixture uses the same local origin and `nosniff`/no-store
  headers as the app API. This avoids engine-dependent buffering/routing in the
  temporary review endpoint; it keeps the real progress assertions.
- Automated contrast/layout checks do not replace a screen-reader usability
  session. Firefox was not run locally. Remote CI covers WebKit as well.
- Hosted feature enablement, Redis-backed hosted paper journeys and the first
  scheduled refresh remain the previously recorded release gates. No flags,
  hosted credentials, storage or production deployment settings were changed.

analysis_refs.heading: Final source and refresh checks
analysis_refs.text:
[HEAD/header-only sampling](evidence/2026-11-01/host-head-checks.json) returned
200 from the textbook, DOAJ publisher, arXiv and Europe PMC hosts. It found a
Gutenberg legacy HTML 404; GET response headers confirmed it. The supplied direct
HTML and EPUB routes returned 200. Importer v2 removes virtual HTML links and
uses supplied direct HTML/landing URLs; a fresh 1,000-record import and runtime
audit passed. The primary location's licence and downloads now stay together;
other hosts/versions retain their own licence, and retraction flags appear on
direct detail visits. No full-text content was stored.

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Search and item resolution
analysis_refs.text:
1. Validate query length, filters, page size (initial max 40), country and cursor binding. Detect ISBN/DOI/arXiv/PMCID before broad search. Country is access context, not legal assurance.
2. Choose providers by user scope/capabilities. Books start from local catalogs; papers use OpenAlex when configured plus at most two relevant specialists. Without the broad index, disclose narrower DOAJ/Europe PMC/arXiv coverage.
3. Use shared cached results. Acquire global quota tokens for uncached requests; arXiv pacing includes all replicas/jobs. Skip with explicit status if the queue cannot run before the deadline.
4. Bound fan-out: proposed 5-second total search deadline, shorter per-provider limits where feasible, at most 3 live providers and one source page each. These are design targets, not measured guarantees. Busy arXiv queues cannot delay every result indefinitely.
5. Map, filter, reconcile and rank. Avoid detail requests for every hit; resolve uncertain access for bounded visible candidates or on item open. Unknown candidates cannot be advertised as free.
6. Return items, source statuses and freshness. Empty, timeout, throttled, quota-exhausted, unsupported and disabled differ. If all sources fail with no local/cached result, return retriable unavailable, not zero matches.
7. On item open, enrich locations as needed; surface editions/versions and host actions. Cache bibliography separately from access observations.

analysis_refs.heading: 2. Twenty categories and how to find candidates for each
analysis_refs.text: | C10 Courses, lecture notes and teaching materials | Open-education consortium members, university OpenCourseWare directories and OER hubs | NPTEL, SWAYAM, IIT/university course portals and teacher-education institutions | Course catalogs/feeds with stable lesson IDs; separate free learning material from paid certificates/enrollment conditions |

analysis_refs.heading: C20 — Educational podcasts, lectures and documentaries
analysis_refs.text:
**Where to start.** Begin with universities, public educational broadcasters and
institutional media producers, following their series/catalog links. In India,
[NPTEL's course catalog](https://nptel.ac.in/courses) provides instructor/course
and institutional discovery leads; investigate official educational broadcaster
and university series alongside it. For international and US material, inspect
university lecture catalogs and public-media learning collections. The
[Internet Archive developer portal](https://archive.org/developers/) documents
metadata tools for archive-hosted media; [Wikimedia Commons API guidance](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Commons:API)
supports another metadata route, with license and exclusion markers to review.

analysis_refs.heading: C20 — Educational podcasts, lectures and documentaries
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval and tests.** Prefer documented catalogs, attributed archive records
or permitted RSS/Atom imports. NPTEL's visible catalog does not establish an
external API in this review. Preserve episode/lecture ID, series/course relation,
producer, language, date, duration and canonical playback URL. Test a complete
recording, removed media, country restriction, premium-only episode and a caption
or transcript where available. Metadata search must not be described as searching
every spoken word. Hosting on an archive or public platform does not establish
lawful free access for every upload. Deep-review one feed-based producer and one
catalog-based producer before selecting a reusable media connector.

analysis_refs.heading: Evidence limits and research handoff
analysis_refs.text:
This pass reviewed official documentation and directory pages on 2026-11-05.
NARA, Archives Portal Europe, National Archives of India, Museums of India,
Bharatavani, Europeana, PRGI, INN/Find Your News, loc.gov, NPTEL, Internet Archive,
Commons and WordPress pages were retrievable. OLAC FAQ and LINCS direct opens
returned 403 despite official search-index descriptions; treat those details as
leads pending direct recheck. Smithsonian `openaccess/devtools` and
`openaccess/faq` opens returned 404 despite indexed results; locate their current
official documentation before qualification. These observations do not establish
service-wide failure or full-item availability.

analysis_refs.heading: C10 — Courses, lecture notes and teaching materials
analysis_refs.text:
For India, [SWAYAM's official overview](https://swayam.gov.in/about) identifies
national coordinators including NPTEL, UGC, CEC, NCERT, NIOS and IGNOU. Follow
coordinator → participating institution → official course/lesson catalog.
Record the producer institution and distribution platform separately. SWAYAM
describes free course learning and paid certification exams; the destination's
actual learning-access conditions still need review.

analysis_refs.text:
In India, start with [DIKSHA's discovery documentation](https://diksha.gov.in/help/getting-started/explore-diksha/),
which describes anonymous exploration and language/location filtering. Follow
the named content organizations to SCERTs, state boards and teacher-training

category membership, not extra origins. The NCERT page returned 502 in this

analysis_refs.heading: C09 — School lessons, curricula and examination resources
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval and tests:** investigate official catalogs, permitted exports or
attributed aggregator coverage. A DIKSHA browser endpoint is not automatically
a supported third-party API. Require item-level board, grade, medium, subject,
curriculum year and canonical resource identity where supplied. Test one lesson
in native script, a retired syllabus, a paper and its answer key, and a topic
shared across different grades. Reject unrelated or obsolete material masquerading
as the current curriculum. Preserve free enrollment versus paid examination rules.

analysis_refs.heading: Hosted release
analysis_refs.text:
No paid service/store was provisioned. Account resources, credentials, activation
and security settings are outside this change. Direct arXiv/DOAJ automation stays
deferred; the UI offers searches at their own websites.

analysis_refs.heading: Current free live profile — 2026-11-03
analysis_refs.text:
One source is queried at a time. Signed native cursors support Show more across
process restarts without server state. Replaying makes another live request;
live indexes can change. Source throttles/timeouts remain explicit. Direct
arXiv/DOAJ automation is deferred; use their source website search links.

analysis_refs.text: | DOAJ | `CONTENT_DOAJ_ENABLED` | `CONTENT_DOAJ_DAILY_LIMIT`, `CONTENT_DOAJ_PER_MINUTE` | At least 500 ms between dispatches across instances |

analysis_refs.heading: Historical shared-store profile (superseded)
analysis_refs.text:
The planner selects at most three live providers. Biomedical terms prefer
Europe PMC; general queries prefer the broad source and arXiv; DOAJ supplies
OA journal coverage. Recognized arXiv identifiers select arXiv. Sources not
chosen are explicit and can be searched independently from the source sheet.
DOIs select DOI-capable indexes; PMCIDs select Europe PMC using its PMCID field,
preserving the article's native MED identity. Bare versioned legacy arXiv IDs
also route directly to arXiv.
Language context is only supported by the broad adapter today; other paper
sources report unsupported rather than silently ignoring it.

analysis_refs.heading: Product requirements
analysis_refs.text:
- Search one selected paper source live. General searches use OpenAlex;
  biomedical searches and PMCIDs use Europe PMC. The Sources sheet switches
  sources. Explicit selection never silently searches a different source.
- Show more carries the provider's paging token in a signed browser token.
  Opening a result resolves its native record directly at that provider.
- No new database, Redis account, paid integration, shared cache or stored search
  session. Existing account features/resources are outside this change.
- Direct arXiv/DOAJ automation stays off because its aggregate pacing rules need
  coordination across deployments. Offer searches on their source websites;
  these connectors do not block other paper sources.
- Keep current source identities, verified free-reading rules, credits, versions,
  separate translations, source errors and browser shelf behavior.

analysis_refs.heading: Multi-source papers follow-up
analysis_refs.text:
DOAJ, arXiv and OpenAlex now have bounded adapters, source-native identities and
per-location access/licence handling. Fresh [policy observations](evidence/2026-11-01/source-policies.json)
verify DOAJ's 2 RPS and arXiv's 3-second/single-connection aggregate rules. The
configured OpenAlex key reported $1/day free allowance, $0.001 ordinary search
and zero prepaid funds; runtime rechecks those conditions before dispatch.
Operational limits and caveats are in [OPERATIONS.md](OPERATIONS.md).

analysis_refs.heading: Final source and refresh checks
analysis_refs.text:
[HEAD/header-only sampling](evidence/2026-11-01/host-head-checks.json) returned
200 from the textbook, DOAJ publisher, arXiv and Europe PMC hosts. It found a
Gutenberg legacy HTML 404; GET response headers confirmed it. The supplied direct
HTML and EPUB routes returned 200. Importer v2 removes virtual HTML links and
uses supplied direct HTML/landing URLs; a fresh 1,000-record import and runtime
audit passed. The primary location's licence and downloads now stay together;
other hosts/versions retain their own licence, and retraction flags appear on
direct detail visits. No full-text content was stored.

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Search and item resolution
analysis_refs.text:
1. Validate query length, filters, page size (initial max 40), country and cursor binding. Detect ISBN/DOI/arXiv/PMCID before broad search. Country is access context, not legal assurance.
2. Choose providers by user scope/capabilities. Books start from local catalogs; papers use OpenAlex when configured plus at most two relevant specialists. Without the broad index, disclose narrower DOAJ/Europe PMC/arXiv coverage.
3. Use shared cached results. Acquire global quota tokens for uncached requests; arXiv pacing includes all replicas/jobs. Skip with explicit status if the queue cannot run before the deadline.
4. Bound fan-out: proposed 5-second total search deadline, shorter per-provider limits where feasible, at most 3 live providers and one source page each. These are design targets, not measured guarantees. Busy arXiv queues cannot delay every result indefinitely.
5. Map, filter, reconcile and rank. Avoid detail requests for every hit; resolve uncertain access for bounded visible candidates or on item open. Unknown candidates cannot be advertised as free.
6. Return items, source statuses and freshness. Empty, timeout, throttled, quota-exhausted, unsupported and disabled differ. If all sources fail with no local/cached result, return retriable unavailable, not zero matches.
7. On item open, enrich locations as needed; surface editions/versions and host actions. Cache bibliography separately from access observations.

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Search and item resolution
Reading actions
analysis_refs.text: Show index and host separately when useful, e.g. Found via DOAJ / Read at publisher. Preserve required attribution. Broken PDF links should fall back to evidenced landing/alternate locations, never invented files. Expose freshness/country limits in details. A public-domain US scan is not a universal legal-access assertion.

analysis_refs.heading: Phase B — initial coverage
analysis_refs.text: Add Open Textbook Library, DOAJ and arXiv; OpenAlex after key/budget verification. Then DOAB/OAPEN imports and optional Unpaywall resolver with real contact email. Keep Google/Open Library enrichment bounded.

analysis_refs.heading: C03 — Published research articles
analysis_refs.text:
**Start with publisher and repository discovery, then prove individual holdings.**
[OpenDOAR](https://opendoar.ac.uk/help/about) supplies institutional repository
leads. [SciELO](https://www.scielo.org/en/) supplies country, publisher and subject
entry points, particularly useful for Latin American and regional-language
coverage. DOAJ remains a directory lead; the current direct DOAJ connector
deferral is unchanged. Separate the publisher, journal collection, repository
copy and index that found it.

analysis_refs.text: Structured responses were obtained from Google Books (using the configured key), Open Library, Internet Archive, DOAJ, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv, Europe PMC, CORE, Zenodo, HAL, Wikisource, Library of Congress, and LibriVox. analysis_refs.heading: What the original checks established
analysis_refs.text:
- An Open Library work returned `ebook_access: public` alongside many Internet Archive identifiers. That does not identify which edition is freely readable.
- A HAL hit had a record URL and DOI but no `fileMain_s`: a repository hit is not necessarily full text.
- Zenodo returned a dataset; item-type filtering is essential.
- DOAJ supplied an older HTTP publisher URL; metadata alone does not prove the destination still works.
- Semantic Scholar returned **429**, and Gutendex timed out. Those checks do not establish general service availability.
- Some documentation URLs moved; corrected DOAB/OAPEN URLs appear in the catalog. Some sites returned only a JavaScript shell. NCERT/ERIC/OER Commons could not be fully inspected.

analysis_refs.heading: Behavior
analysis_refs.text:
Wikipedia, Wikibooks and Wikisource remain disconnected: the current robots
policies disallow the reviewed `/w/api.php` search route. No alternate route was
used to evade this restriction. arXiv/DOAJ retain their existing pacing-related
exclusion from live requests. Other registry candidates require supported query,
access or credential work before integration. This release does not make an
unverified directory or research lead searchable by merely listing it.

analysis_refs.heading: 1. Goal and counting rules
analysis_refs.text:
Use 20 research categories: five core areas and 15 additions. Target 100 qualified
sources per category over successive research cycles. These are overlapping
category memberships, potentially 2,000 memberships, not necessarily 2,000 unique
sources or 2,000 custom integrations. Report the global unique count separately.

analysis_refs.heading: 3. Discovery engines to use before broad web searching
analysis_refs.text:
Also investigate DOAJ, CORE/OpenAIRE/BASE, national libraries, professional
associations and ministry directories as leads. Choose an aggregator only after
checking current external-use terms, quotas, origin attribution and completeness.
Existing direct arXiv/DOAJ deferral remains in force until its stated constraint
has a supported solution; this plan does not quietly re-enable those connectors.

analysis_refs.heading: C02. General books and ebooks
analysis_refs.text:
**Best starting points.** [Project Gutenberg's official catalog documentation](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/offline_catalogs.html)
identifies machine-readable catalogs, OPDS and affiliate/mirror links. Use the
catalog as a retrieval model; mirrors are duplicate hosting. National libraries,
state digital libraries, regional literary organizations and university special
collections supply additional independent origins. The [Library of Congress
JSON/YAML interface](https://www.loc.gov/apis/json-and-yaml/) is a US starting
point for digitized collection records; its scope is not the entire library catalog.
DPLA's [developer documentation](https://pro.dp.la/developers/api-codex) is a
US aggregator lead requiring a fresh documentation/access check before selection.

analysis_refs.heading: C14 — Language learning and adult literacy
analysis_refs.text:
**Where to start.** The [Open Language Archives Community](https://www.language-archives.org/)
provides a language-resource discovery network; its
[FAQ](https://www.language-archives.org/documents/faq/) describes participating
archives and OAI metadata exchange. Filter for instructional materials: a
linguistic recording or restricted research corpus is not automatically a usable
language lesson. For US adult literacy, the
[LINCS resource collection](https://lincs.ed.gov/resource-collection) identifies
instructional producers and state/local program resources. In India,
[Bharatavani](https://www.bharatavani.in/home/dictionaries) identifies dictionaries,
glossaries, languages and contributing institutions; follow those producers to
their lesson, primer and literacy catalogs. Also investigate state literacy
missions and university language departments through official institution sites.

analysis_refs.heading: C16 — Museums, art and cultural heritage
analysis_refs.text:
**Where to start.** [Europeana's API overview](https://www.europeana.eu/en/apis)
describes search, record and harvesting routes with contributing institutions.
Use provider attribution to discover museums across countries, then check the
institution's own open-collection policy. In India,
[Museums of India's digitization initiative](https://museumsofindia.gov.in/repository/page/digitization_initiative)
links participating museums, with JATAN as the collection-management context.
This is a useful network of leads; it does not establish a public integration API.
For the US investigate museum open-access programs and official collection
developer pages, including Smithsonian as a lead requiring renewed documentation.

**Where to start.** Begin with universities, public educational broadcasters and
institutional media producers, following their series/catalog links. In India,
[NPTEL's course catalog](https://nptel.ac.in/courses) provides instructor/course
and institutional discovery leads; investigate official educational broadcaster
and university series alongside it. For international and US material, inspect
university lecture catalogs and public-media learning collections. The
[Internet Archive developer portal](https://archive.org/developers/) documents
metadata tools for archive-hosted media; [Wikimedia Commons API guidance](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Commons:API)
supports another metadata route, with license and exclusion markers to review.

analysis_refs.heading: 4. Source registry and adapters
analysis_refs.text: Unpaywall implements `locate`, not search. Crossref enriches bibliography. OAI implements `harvest` and feeds a local-index search adapter. Unsupported filters must be rejected or disclosed, never silently ignored while presenting supposedly filtered results.

analysis_refs.heading: Phase B — initial coverage
analysis_refs.text: Add Open Textbook Library, DOAJ and arXiv; OpenAlex after key/budget verification. Then DOAB/OAPEN imports and optional Unpaywall resolver with real contact email. Keep Google/Open Library enrichment bounded.

analysis_refs.heading: What the original checks established
analysis_refs.text: Two current details make older integration advice unreliable: Standard Ebooks' full OPDS feeds require membership/access arrangements, and Unpaywall's documentation said its title-search endpoint retired on **2026-09-18**. Use Unpaywall for DOI resolution and another index for search. Recheck these policies before implementation.

analysis_refs.heading: Credentials and implementation inputs
analysis_refs.text:
1. Verify **`OPENALEX_API_KEY`** in the backend. The replacement environment reports the variable configured; no authenticated OpenAlex request was made during this repository transfer. At the research date the free account included $1/day of API usage, roughly 1,000 ordinary search requests before caching. Disable paid overages unless deliberately budgeted.
2. Choose a real **application contact email** for request identification and, if enabled, Unpaywall's required `email` parameter. No email was invented, registered, or sent during this work.
3. Optional later: Semantic Scholar, BHL and Europeana keys; CORE upgrade/eligibility confirmation. Standard Ebooks feed access and children's/OER catalog feeds need provider-specific arrangements.

analysis_refs.heading: From a directory entry to something the app can query
analysis_refs.text:
1. **Official document/dataset catalog API.** [GovInfo documents an API search
   service](https://www.govinfo.gov/features/search-service-overview) for content
   and metadata. The current [Data.gov Catalog API](https://resources.data.gov/catalog-api/)
   searches dataset metadata and identifies publisher organizations; it explicitly
   replaces the previous CKAN API. Use the current interface and key policy,
   not an old tutorial. An indexed dataset still needs a valid resource link.
2. **Approved exports and local metadata search.** Small DCAT/CSV/JSON/XML catalogs
   can become bounded, reviewed search artifacts without a hosted database. Prefer
   metadata and canonical outbound links; do not copy whole national parcel or
   imagery stores to make a prototype searchable.
3. **Native record or feature queries.** A source can qualify for property or
   spatial lookup through real address/parcel/document-ID/area queries even when
   it lacks general keyword search. This must return record metadata and a usable
   destination; an identifier-shaped redirect to an external search page is not
   retrieval. Record this as a separate capability from topic discovery.
4. **Geo services with explicit discovery.** [OGC WFS](https://www.ogc.org/standards/wfs/),
   [OGC API Features](https://www.ogc.org/standards/ogcapi-features/) and documented
   [ArcGIS layer queries](https://developers.arcgis.com/rest/services-reference/enterprise/query-feature-service-layer/)
   are patterns to inspect for spatial/attribute filtering. Confirm the deployed
   service's capabilities, limits, IDs and terms; the platform brand is not proof.
   [WMS](https://www.ogc.org/standards/wms/)/WMTS primarily deliver rendered maps
   or tiles. A searchable layer catalog can support map discovery, but does not
   establish searchable parcel attributes or downloadable source features.

analysis_refs.text:
**All records are samples.** Project Gutenberg IDs, titles and the Gutenberg
rights wording are real. Every paper, author, journal, DOI (the `10.5555` test
prefix), arXiv ID and children's story is invented. Never copy board records
into fixtures as if they were real catalog data.

analysis_refs.heading: 2. Scope
analysis_refs.text:
- Free to read: Project Gutenberg (local metadata import), Open Textbook
  Library and the bounded Book Dash catalog (owner-approved source expansion). Other free versions (LibriVox, Wikisource) appear only on detail
  pages as separate items, when a source links them.
- Papers: OpenAlex (when its key and budget are verified), Europe PMC, DOAJ,
  arXiv.
- Children's stories: the reviewed pilot set only, labelled as such.
- The library book page gains an "Also free to read" section.
- Desktop and mobile layouts, all three reading lights.

analysis_refs.heading: 4. Boards
analysis_refs.text: | `FreeBookResults` | Results for a free-book query, filter chips, loaded count with a Sources link, and the hidden-unclear notice. | Show **loaded counts**, never a global total ("3 free books shown · from Project Gutenberg"). Anonymous `free_full_text` items and a separately labelled `free_account_required` group are listed. Items with `unknown`/`metadata_only` access for this query are counted in the notice; "Show them, labelled" appends them under an "Unclear access" heading (see `DeskFreeSearch`). `preview`, `borrow`, unknown-price `registration` and `restricted` are never shown. Verified free accounts follow the owner clarification above. Filter chips: language, format, kind. Unsupported filters must be disabled with a reason, not silently ignored. |

analysis_refs.heading: 7. Copy and accessibility rules
analysis_refs.text:
- Keep "free to read" separate from reuse rights in all copy. "Free" means free
  to read at the source, never "free to download and share".
- Failures are never absence: timeout, limit, down and unsupported states each
  have their own copy; none says "no results".
- Name the host in every outbound action ("Read at Project Gutenberg").
- Status is conveyed by text plus shape (filled vs hollow dot, pill label), not
  colour alone. Check contrast in Daylight, Lamplight and Ink.
- Live regions: loading progress `role="status"` (polite); `SourcesDown`
  `role="alert"`.
- Respect reduced motion; boards use no animation and the app shouldn't add any
  for these states.
- Language chips and story titles in Hindi/Tamil carry `lang`.

analysis_refs.heading: C02. General books and ebooks
analysis_refs.text:
**Best starting points.** [Project Gutenberg's official catalog documentation](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/offline_catalogs.html)
identifies machine-readable catalogs, OPDS and affiliate/mirror links. Use the
catalog as a retrieval model; mirrors are duplicate hosting. National libraries,
state digital libraries, regional literary organizations and university special
collections supply additional independent origins. The [Library of Congress
JSON/YAML interface](https://www.loc.gov/apis/json-and-yaml/) is a US starting
point for digitized collection records; its scope is not the entire library catalog.
DPLA's [developer documentation](https://pro.dp.la/developers/api-codex) is a
US aggregator lead requiring a fresh documentation/access check before selection.

analysis_refs.text:
537 server tests with real Redis/no skips, 141 client tests, 262 broad browser
journeys, 50 final feature journeys and 84 axe/overflow capture checks pass, with
typecheck/build/SEO/deployment. The actual Tamil StoryWeaver and Book Dash app
flows pass again through save/reload/reopen. Source data and hosted release gates
are unchanged. Consult the PR for CI at the current commit.

Official Gutenberg/OTL/Book Dash refreshes retain all 1,000/1,909/30 native keys,

analysis_refs.heading: Historical shared-store profile (superseded)
analysis_refs.text:
All flags default off. No hosted Redis service or production deployment has
been created by this implementation. Gutenberg, Open Textbook Library and Book Dash use
bundled metadata and require no database. The reviewed StoryWeaver set also
searches locally, including ordinary Free to read searches when its flag is on. Live paper sources need the shared
Redis REST URL/token and a strong random `CONTENT_CURSOR_SECRET` (at least 32
characters), plus an explicit daily/minute budget for each enabled source.
The build's `VITE_CONTENT_DISCOVERY_ENABLED` controls the Search scopes.

analysis_refs.heading: Enablement
analysis_refs.text:
Enable `CONTENT_DISCOVERY_ENABLED`, `CONTENT_CHILDREN_ENABLED`,
`VITE_CONTENT_DISCOVERY_ENABLED` and `VITE_CHILDREN_PILOT_ENABLED` for the checked
preview/production build, with separate strong server-only cursor signing secrets.
This publishes Gutenberg, Open Textbook Library, Book Dash and the reviewed
StoryWeaver set. Source-account requirements remain visible.

analysis_refs.heading: Evidence and limits
analysis_refs.text:
- The comparison fixtures are explicitly synthetic for papers/stories; they do
  not establish source access or represent the actual reviewed children's set.
  Their metadata is isolated in `client/e2e/free-content-ui-fixture.js`.
- The [actual-source app flows](evidence/2026-11-01/ui-review/actual-source-flow/expanded-sources-app-flow.json)
  separately exercise the real Tamil StoryWeaver record and Book Dash edition:
  search → detail → supplied source URL → save → reload → reopen, on desktop and
  phone, including 320px/200% text. Their credits and free-account condition are
  preserved. No source account was created and post-login reading is untested.
- Sources, counts, levels and available relations differ from the board samples.
  Only source-supplied versions/downloads/relations render; no v1/v2 list, recording,
  translation, cover art or licence is inferred to imitate sample data.
- The shared four-tab shell, desktop navigation rail and browser safe-area
  handling remain the existing app. The source sheet keeps its shared Close
  control. Catalog-subset disclosure and the owner-approved free-account group
  add necessary content beyond the original sample boards.
- Recent query history is bounded and lost on reload. It is not written to
  local storage, an account, analytics or a server history store.
- A fresh Europe PMC request on the current local API exceeded the five-second
  source deadline. The actual UI rendered an unavailable alert and no empty-copy
  claim. Earlier successful live-paper flows remain dated evidence, not a claim
  that the external service answered this later probe.
- The streamed-loading fixture uses the same local origin and `nosniff`/no-store
  headers as the app API. This avoids engine-dependent buffering/routing in the
  temporary review endpoint; it keeps the real progress assertions.
- Automated contrast/layout checks do not replace a screen-reader usability
  session. Firefox was not run locally. Remote CI covers WebKit as well.
- Hosted feature enablement, Redis-backed hosted paper journeys and the first
  scheduled refresh remain the previously recorded release gates. No flags,
  hosted credentials, storage or production deployment settings were changed.

creator credits. Both flowed without Redis, page errors or horizontal overflow

[Tamil phone detail](evidence/2026-11-01/children-reviewed-detail-phone.png) and
[Book Dash desktop search/detail](evidence/2026-11-01/bookdash-detail-desktop.png).

audit. A second real refresh used pinned native IDs and retained all 30; newer
catalog entries cannot evict saved editions from the bounded subset. Import tests
cover source-only URLs/language/credits/galleries, metadata-only output, failed

loaded all 14 supplied pages. No book artwork/text or guessed downloads enter the

not a worldwide catalog size or a search-match total. Eight sources have
implementations: these four book sources plus four existing live paper adapters.

analysis_refs.heading: The ten candidates
analysis_refs.text:
This is ten discovery options, not ten demonstrated net-new origins in production.
GDL and BHL aggregate contributors; do not add their contributor counts on top.
BHL's Internet Archive hosting is not another source. Measure item/publisher
overlap with existing StoryWeaver, Book Dash, OTL and Gutenberg before reporting
incremental coverage. The five named publishers have distinct publisher IDs;
their chapters, editions and mirrored files do not increase that count.

analysis_refs.heading: C01. Children's books and early literacy
analysis_refs.text:
**Best starting points.** [IBBY national sections](https://www.ibby.org/ibby-worldwide/ibby-sections)
provide country-level publishing/literacy networks, including India and the US.
Follow sections to publishers and literacy organizations with digital collections.
For India, [Parag's publisher and bookstore directory](https://www.paragreads.in/parag-reads/childrens-publishers-and-bookstores/)
is a concrete seed list; bookstores and commercial catalogs remain leads rather
than eligible sources. [Book Dash's partner network](https://bookdash.org/partners/)
links literacy organizations and content collaborators, including African
Storybook and Pratham Books. Distinguish content producers from organizations
that only distribute another publisher's books.

analysis_refs.heading: C01. Children's books and early literacy
analysis_refs.text:
**First ten leads:** four India-origin publishers/NGOs from Parag and Pratham
connections, four publishers from other IBBY sections, and two independent
catalogs identified through Book Dash collaborators. Deduplicate shared catalogs;
deep-review one reusable-feed candidate and one multilingual candidate first.

analysis_refs.text:

tool returned HTTP 402 for StoryWeaver's open-content page, 502 for NCERT's
textbook page and 403 for DPLA's API page. Sugamya redirected to its current domain
but exposed no readable content to the tool. These observations establish neither
payment requirements nor source-wide outages. No credentials, source accounts,
outreach, bulk harvests or live query qualification probes were performed.

This is an unresolved provider/runtime reliability observation, not a zero-result claim. The mobile WebKit all-source query completed all 16 groups with 26 loaded results, no page errors and no horizontal overflow; the LibriVox detail linked to the correct recording. See [saved production evidence](evidence/knowledge-release-2026-11-05/production/deployment.json), including failed probes and screenshots. analysis_refs.text: | **Open Library — index linking to hosts** | `/search.json`, work/edition JSON; title, author, ISBN, language, ebook fields. analysis_refs.heading: Recommendation
analysis_refs.text: Reuse Google Books and Open Library selectively to enrich book records and resolve existing saved books to candidate free editions. Their general catalogs contain previews, borrowing offers, and metadata-only records; they should not define the free-reading collection by themselves.

analysis_refs.heading: 3. Discovery engines to use before broad web searching
analysis_refs.text:
Documentation review limitations on 2026-11-05: the older DOAB metadata URL
returned 404; the linked `doab-metadata` page worked. AISHE and data.gov.in opens
timed out; DOAJ/CORE documentation opens returned 403 in this research tool.
Those remain leads, not verified integrations or evidence that the services are
down. No source-search API qualification probes were run for this plan.

analysis_refs.heading: 10. Progress report and immediate next batch
analysis_refs.text:
The content categories are accepted. The next research cycle uses M1 across all
20 categories and 20 industry tags with the six playbooks. In M2,
prioritize book/education/India opportunities plus US/India public records/maps
and practical industry documentation: DOAB/OAPEN publisher coverage,
national/regional literature catalogs, school textbook bodies, children's
publishers, thesis repositories, audiobook catalogs, official civic/property
catalogs, geological data and agriculture/construction/manufacturing/logistics
guidance. Recheck existing source
freshness first; new names do not solve an expired catalog or a three-item pilot.

analysis_refs.heading: Phase B — initial coverage
analysis_refs.text: Add Open Textbook Library, DOAJ and arXiv; OpenAlex after key/budget verification. Then DOAB/OAPEN imports and optional Unpaywall resolver with real contact email. Keep Google/Open Library enrichment bounded.

analysis_refs.heading: C04. Textbooks and scholarly books/chapters
analysis_refs.text:
**Best starting points.** [DOAB metadata](https://doabooks.org/en/librarians/doab-metadata)
documents CC0 exports and OAI-PMH, including selective publisher/subject exports.
Use publisher identities to discover origins and verify their actual OA subsets.
[Open Textbook Library discovery](https://open.umn.edu/opentextbooks/discovery)
documents MARC/CSV, JSON resources and change feeds. Follow textbook publisher and
institution links into university presses and open-education programs. These
catalogs expose different kinds of books; keep textbooks, monographs and chapters
distinct even when the same publisher supplies all three.

analysis_refs.heading: C04. Textbooks and scholarly books/chapters
analysis_refs.text:
**Search process.** Enumerate publisher-origin candidates from approved metadata
exports by discipline, language and geography; inspect batches of 25 distinct
publishers. Search `"{university press}" "open access books"`,
`"{subject}" "open textbook" "{country}"`, and
`site:{education-body-domain} (textbook OR publication) (catalog OR download)`.
Follow open-education network members into their own catalogs and compare against
DOAB/OTL holdings. To approach 100, add qualified publisher catalogs across
disciplines, not 100 series from one press. Record the fraction actually covered
by the aggregator; a few OA titles never imply a wholly free publisher catalog.

analysis_refs.heading: C04. Textbooks and scholarly books/chapters
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval to investigate.** Prefer DOAB/OTL-origin mapping and official exports
before custom publisher connectors. OAI-PMH needs an import and local keyword
index; it is not a topic-search API. Per-book licenses and destinations remain
separate from the metadata feed license. Verify withdrawn records, corrected
editions and bounded refresh costs without provisioning a hosted database.

analysis_refs.heading: C04. Textbooks and scholarly books/chapters
analysis_refs.text:
**First ten leads:** four Indian educational publishers/institutions, four new
publishers represented in DOAB/OTL, and two independently maintained catalogs from
underrepresented regions. Deep-review a publisher represented by an export and
an India school-text catalog to compare integration and refresh effort.

analysis_refs.heading: Evidence boundaries and next handoff
analysis_refs.text:
Documentation opens succeeded for IBBY, Parag, Book Dash, Gutenberg, OTL, DOAB,
Project Madurai, LibriVox, DAISY and NLS during this planning review. The research
tool returned HTTP 402 for StoryWeaver's open-content page, 502 for NCERT's
textbook page and 403 for DPLA's API page. Sugamya redirected to its current domain
but exposed no readable content to the tool. These observations establish neither
payment requirements nor source-wide outages. No credentials, source accounts,
outreach, bulk harvests or live query qualification probes were performed.

analysis_refs.heading: The ten candidates
analysis_refs.text:
This is ten discovery options, not ten demonstrated net-new origins in production.
GDL and BHL aggregate contributors; do not add their contributor counts on top.
BHL's Internet Archive hosting is not another source. Measure item/publisher
overlap with existing StoryWeaver, Book Dash, OTL and Gutenberg before reporting
incremental coverage. The five named publishers have distinct publisher IDs;
their chapters, editions and mirrored files do not increase that count.

analysis_refs.heading: Query behavior and operating constraints
analysis_refs.text:
All six retrieval families—GDL, MediaWiki, LoC JSON, Internet Archive search,
LibriVox and Thoth—were probed with a nonsense term. Empty results were observed;
LibriVox expresses this as HTTP 404 with an audiobook-not-found JSON message.
An adapter must distinguish that documented response shape from an outage.
Representative second-page requests were also checked; retain each provider's
paging and scope. These checks are evidence, not implemented app behavior.

analysis_refs.heading: Query behavior and operating constraints
analysis_refs.text:
No paid fallback is proposed. All tested search requests worked anonymously.
Respect current provider limits and use bounded requests, cancellation, backoff
and truthful unavailable states. No numeric unlimited allowance is inferred where
documentation does not publish one. Wikimedia calls should be serial with a
descriptive User-Agent and maxlag for research; Internet Archive also requests
identification of automated clients. LibriVox documents a maximum page size of
500 and pacing for bulk work. We requested only three catalog records at a time,
except GDL's fixed 20-record search page.

analysis_refs.heading: C20 — Educational podcasts, lectures and documentaries
analysis_refs.text:
**Where to start.** Begin with universities, public educational broadcasters and
institutional media producers, following their series/catalog links. In India,
[NPTEL's course catalog](https://nptel.ac.in/courses) provides instructor/course
and institutional discovery leads; investigate official educational broadcaster
and university series alongside it. For international and US material, inspect
university lecture catalogs and public-media learning collections. The
[Internet Archive developer portal](https://archive.org/developers/) documents
metadata tools for archive-hosted media; [Wikimedia Commons API guidance](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Commons:API)
supports another metadata route, with license and exclusion markers to review.

analysis_refs.heading: What the original checks established
analysis_refs.text: Structured responses were obtained from Google Books (using the configured key), Open Library, Internet Archive, DOAJ, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv, Europe PMC, CORE, Zenodo, HAL, Wikisource, Library of Congress, and LibriVox. Gutenberg RDF and DOAB record/harvesting responses also worked. OAPEN's OAI service identification worked; a record import was not exercised.

analysis_refs.heading: What the original checks established
analysis_refs.text:
- An Open Library work returned `ebook_access: public` alongside many Internet Archive identifiers. That does not identify which edition is freely readable.
- A HAL hit had a record URL and DOI but no `fileMain_s`: a repository hit is not necessarily full text.
- Zenodo returned a dataset; item-type filtering is essential.
- DOAJ supplied an older HTTP publisher URL; metadata alone does not prove the destination still works.
- Semantic Scholar returned **429**, and Gutendex timed out. Those checks do not establish general service availability.
- Some documentation URLs moved; corrected DOAB/OAPEN URLs appear in the catalog. Some sites returned only a JavaScript shell. NCERT/ERIC/OER Commons could not be fully inspected.

analysis_refs.heading: Behavior

Ten new integrations are released behind `CONTENT_KNOWLEDGE_ENABLED=true`:
Global Digital Library, LibriVox, Library of Congress digital books, Biodiversity
Heritage Library's Internet Archive collection, African Minds, LSE Press,
Mattering Press, mediastudies.press, punctum books and Python 3.15 documentation.
Five publisher catalogs share Thoth; this is not five separate API infrastructures.
The existing Gutenberg, Open Textbook Library, Book Dash and StoryWeaver snapshots
and the existing OpenAlex/Europe PMC integrations are also selectable. With the
existing production flags, this gives 16 connected sources, not 16 fully audited
origins or complete catalogs.

analysis_refs.text:
Refresh operational health and access evidence separately from long-term source
policy reviews. Use each source's documented limits/change cadence; monthly
directory gap reviews and periodic policy checks are planning defaults, not a
reason to hammer every endpoint daily. Suspend failing source actions honestly.

analysis_refs.heading: FCD01: contract decisions
analysis_refs.text:
- Content keys use `fcd:v1:<source>:<record>`; Gutenberg records are positive
  integer IDs; Europe PMC records include their source (`MED`, `PMC`, `PPR`).
  A DOI is an identifier, never an app key. Versions, translations, chapters and
  recordings retain distinct source-native keys. No fuzzy-title merge.
- Reviewed StoryWeaver translations use distinct native story IDs. The pilot
  requires English/Hindi/Tamil records with original credits, publisher levels
  and per-record review evidence before enablement.
- An omitted `kinds` searches books/learning resources. Paper searches supply
  paper kinds explicitly. Mixed book/paper requests are reported unsupported;
  the API never silently omits one requested scope.
- Search and resolve both accept `country` (ISO alpha-2 or absent/unknown) and
  language context. An observation for one explicit country does not establish
  availability in another. Gutenberg's US rights statement is retained with a
  generic country-rules prompt, not turned into a global legal claim.
- A reading action requires an explicit per-location `free_full_text` claim,
  positive evidence field/source/time, a safe supplied HTTP(S) URL, and an
  observation no older than 24 hours. Stale, missing, contradictory or
  country-mismatched observations become unknown; fetch failure is not absence.
  Reuse licence and free reading remain distinct. Missing licence never becomes
  an invented Creative Commons licence.
- `not_selected` means the planner did not query this source; `disabled` means
  it is not connected. `ok` with zero results is distinct from timeout,
  unavailable, throttled and quota-exhausted. Counts describe loaded items,
  never a federated global total.
- Default results contain anonymous free full text and a separately labelled verified free-account group (owner clarification 2026-11-01). An explicit unclear group may
  contain unknown/metadata-only items with labelled source links; previews,
  borrowing, unknown-price registration and restricted access stay excluded in v1.
- Source cursors remain server-owned. Browser tokens bind query, context,
  policy/index revisions and expiry. Shared live quota reservation and page
  advancement must pass a two-instance test before a live source is enabled.
  A memory implementation is a development/test adapter only; store failure
  disables uncapped live dispatch while keeping local metadata searchable.

journeys, 50 final feature journeys and 84 axe/overflow capture checks pass, with

flows pass again through save/reload/reopen. Source data and hosted release gates
are unchanged. Consult the PR for CI at the current commit.

Official Gutenberg/OTL/Book Dash refreshes retain all 1,000/1,909/30 native keys,
with zero semantic metadata changes. Current evidence supports 987/1,905/30
reading actions. These are bounded catalog counts, not global source totals.
The StoryWeaver reading-offer recheck failed; its previous observations are
retained, never renewed manually. #127 tracks that separate source-review gate.

analysis_refs.heading: Historical shared-store profile (superseded)
analysis_refs.text:
All flags default off. No hosted Redis service or production deployment has
been created by this implementation. Gutenberg, Open Textbook Library and Book Dash use
bundled metadata and require no database. The reviewed StoryWeaver set also
searches locally, including ordinary Free to read searches when its flag is on. Live paper sources need the shared
Redis REST URL/token and a strong random `CONTENT_CURSOR_SECRET` (at least 32
characters), plus an explicit daily/minute budget for each enabled source.
The build's `VITE_CONTENT_DISCOVERY_ENABLED` controls the Search scopes.

analysis_refs.heading: Reviewed source-account books
analysis_refs.text:
The three reviewed StoryWeaver books require `CONTENT_CHILDREN_ENABLED=true`
(and the normal discovery flag); the children's browse tile additionally uses
`VITE_CHILDREN_PILOT_ENABLED=true`. No source account or reader credentials are
stored by MyBookshelf. Source review/refresh instructions are in
[CHILDREN_REVIEW.md](CHILDREN_REVIEW.md). The refresh workflow checks these records
in a browser and refuses changed credits/levels, unknown charges or failed policy
checks. It proposes metadata; it never promotes production.

analysis_refs.heading: Enablement
analysis_refs.text:
Enable `CONTENT_DISCOVERY_ENABLED`, `CONTENT_CHILDREN_ENABLED`,
`VITE_CONTENT_DISCOVERY_ENABLED` and `VITE_CHILDREN_PILOT_ENABLED` for the checked
preview/production build, with separate strong server-only cursor signing secrets.
This publishes Gutenberg, Open Textbook Library, Book Dash and the reviewed
StoryWeaver set. Source-account requirements remain visible.

analysis_refs.heading: Verification
analysis_refs.text:
The four local book sources remain bounded metadata catalogs. Paper enablement
still depends on owner-deferred Redis; #127 separately tracks the GitHub
StoryWeaver refresh prompt failure. No source-observation timestamps are renewed
by this search fix.

analysis_refs.heading: Evidence and limits
analysis_refs.text:
- The comparison fixtures are explicitly synthetic for papers/stories; they do
  not establish source access or represent the actual reviewed children's set.
  Their metadata is isolated in `client/e2e/free-content-ui-fixture.js`.
- The [actual-source app flows](evidence/2026-11-01/ui-review/actual-source-flow/expanded-sources-app-flow.json)
  separately exercise the real Tamil StoryWeaver record and Book Dash edition:
  search → detail → supplied source URL → save → reload → reopen, on desktop and
  phone, including 320px/200% text. Their credits and free-account condition are
  preserved. No source account was created and post-login reading is untested.
- Sources, counts, levels and available relations differ from the board samples.
  Only source-supplied versions/downloads/relations render; no v1/v2 list, recording,
  translation, cover art or licence is inferred to imitate sample data.
- The shared four-tab shell, desktop navigation rail and browser safe-area
  handling remain the existing app. The source sheet keeps its shared Close
  control. Catalog-subset disclosure and the owner-approved free-account group
  add necessary content beyond the original sample boards.
- Recent query history is bounded and lost on reload. It is not written to
  local storage, an account, analytics or a server history store.
- A fresh Europe PMC request on the current local API exceeded the five-second
  source deadline. The actual UI rendered an unavailable alert and no empty-copy
  claim. Earlier successful live-paper flows remain dated evidence, not a claim
  that the external service answered this later probe.
- The streamed-loading fixture uses the same local origin and `nosniff`/no-store
  headers as the app API. This avoids engine-dependent buffering/routing in the
  temporary review endpoint; it keeps the real progress assertions.
- Automated contrast/layout checks do not replace a screen-reader usability
  session. Firefox was not run locally. Remote CI covers WebKit as well.
- Hosted feature enablement, Redis-backed hosted paper journeys and the first
  scheduled refresh remain the previously recorded release gates. No flags,
  hosted credentials, storage or production deployment settings were changed.

analysis_refs.heading: Remaining release gates
analysis_refs.text:
- Hosted shared Redis REST binding and explicit per-source budgets; flags remain
  off without them. Local Gutenberg search requires no database.
- Reviewed real children’s metadata and local app journeys are now complete.
  The three StoryWeaver books require a free source account, as accepted by the
  owner; no source account was created and post-login reading was not tested.
- Automated reviewed catalog refresh before 24-hour access evidence expiry;
  the candidate tool/daily draft-PR workflow are now implemented and tested
  locally; first scheduled execution follows default-branch merge. Stale evidence
  remains unknown. No global Gutenberg/OTL completeness or deletion claim.
- Finish board-state coverage, source-specific retraction/version fixtures,
  fresh protected preview and final hosted release checks. WebKit runs in CI;
  Firefox is not part of the existing CI browser matrix and has not been run here.

analysis_refs.heading: Free source accounts and additional source delivery
analysis_refs.text:
The owner explicitly accepted free source login and assigned source research to
Codex. Public StoryWeaver metadata loaded in a normal browser even though direct
requests were blocked. Actual Read Story controls for records 7, 8 and 2252
returned 401 and a free signup offer. They are searchable as
`free_account_required`, grouped separately and labelled again before the source
reading link. Generic/unknown-price registration remains excluded. Explicit
`access: free_full_text` API requests remain anonymous-only. Old evidence becomes
unknown, and account-conditioned actions never invent direct file downloads.

analysis_refs.heading: Free source accounts and additional source delivery
analysis_refs.text:
Current real-source records: 1,000 Gutenberg, 1,909 textbook, 30 Book Dash and
three reviewed StoryWeaver records. This is 2,942 bounded metadata records,
not a worldwide catalog size or a search-match total. Eight sources have
implementations: these four book sources plus four existing live paper adapters.
The OpenAlex key was rechecked successfully. Redis remains deferred by the owner;
no hosted store, source account or production enablement was created here.

analysis_refs.heading: Phase C — children, regional and specialist coverage
analysis_refs.text: Reviewed children's pilot with approved metadata, attribution, language and level. Obtain feeds for comprehensive StoryWeaver/African Storybook/Book Dash search. Add CORE/HAL/Zenodo and India-specific providers in response to measured gaps; audio optional.

analysis_refs.heading: The ten candidates
analysis_refs.text:
This is ten discovery options, not ten demonstrated net-new origins in production.
GDL and BHL aggregate contributors; do not add their contributor counts on top.
BHL's Internet Archive hosting is not another source. Measure item/publisher
overlap with existing StoryWeaver, Book Dash, OTL and Gutenberg before reporting
incremental coverage. The five named publishers have distinct publisher IDs;
their chapters, editions and mirrored files do not increase that count.

analysis_refs.heading: Reading evidence and source-specific limits
analysis_refs.text: | GDL | English **Rain** page exposed 15 H5P chapter/page units; Hindi sample exposed 19, without login. Both had actual embedded book content rather than only catalog cards. | Some publisher/credit fields are empty in API responses: recover evidence from the book's attribution data. Per-book CC licenses differ. The `rain` result set also included **Queens of Shakrain**, so native substring search needs relevance checks. Avoid double-counting StoryWeaver/other republished stories. |

analysis_refs.heading: C01. Children's books and early literacy
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval to investigate.** Prefer attributed coverage in an approved catalog,
an official export, or a supported publisher interface. An open-source website
codebase does not grant API access or metadata reuse. Free reader registration is
acceptable when disclosed; an advertised offer and verified post-login access are
separate observations. Recheck the existing StoryWeaver gate before expanding it.

analysis_refs.heading: Evidence boundaries and next handoff
analysis_refs.text:
Documentation opens succeeded for IBBY, Parag, Book Dash, Gutenberg, OTL, DOAB,
Project Madurai, LibriVox, DAISY and NLS during this planning review. The research
tool returned HTTP 402 for StoryWeaver's open-content page, 502 for NCERT's
textbook page and 403 for DPLA's API page. Sugamya redirected to its current domain
but exposed no readable content to the tool. These observations establish neither
payment requirements nor source-wide outages. No credentials, source accounts,
outreach, bulk harvests or live query qualification probes were performed.
